findings.title: Use persisted enabled state when deciding login-cache invalidation
findings.body: The original model passed to this method comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when its organization (or organization support in the realm) is disabled. The login query, however, caches IDs based on the persisted IDP fields. For example, populate the cache for a public enabled organization IDP, disable its organization, then set hideOnLogin=true on the IDP. Both predicates here return false, so the cached membership is retained. After re-enabling the organization, getForLogin still returns that hidden IDP, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so it displays the provider despite hideOnLogin. Compare unwrapped persisted models for invalidation rather than organization-dependent enabled state.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual created provider aliases
findings.body: The new test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19 but registers every cleanup against the literal provider name "alias"; the same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. Cleanup therefore attempts to delete a nonexistent provider instead of the created resources, potentially failing teardown and leaving realm-level providers behind to contaminate later tests. Register each created alias in its cleanup callback.
